newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's oil refinery seeks Korean investment.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's oil refinery seeks Korean investment.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftohim has started talks with South Korean refiners on attracting much-needed investment for modernisation, industry sources said on Monday.
"We are expecting South Korean officials to come to Bulgaria soon and continue talks," a Neftohim official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
She said talks had started last week during the visit of Neftohim's executive director Stefan Nedelchev to South Korean refineries.
Nedelchev was not immediately available for comment.
Officials said investment was needed for upgrading the reforming installations and the Neftohim management was looking forward to starting negotiations with a South Korean refinery.
Neftohim plans to invest some $130 million in modernisation projects by the year 2005 to cope with an expected increase in output and a switch to unleaded gasoline production.

Apart from an expected annual rise of 4-5 percent in domestic consumption within the next 10 years, the plant may also refine Russian crude to be delivered via a planned tanker route from Russia to Greece, a government official said.

Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan to supply Russian crude by tankers from Russia's Black Sea port of Novorosiisk to Bourgas in Bulgaria from where a new pipeline would carry the crude Alexandroupolis in Greece.
